title: Counterfactual Fairness Evaluation of LLM-Based Contact Center Agent Quality Assurance System

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of agent names and pronouns in contact center transcripts to measure binary judgment reversals (Counterfactual Flip Rate) and score shifts (Mean Absolute Score Difference).
Counterfactual substitution of culturally coded names and the injection of dialect or linguistic markers into conversational turns to measure evaluation disparities.
Counterfactual substitution of religiously identifiable names and the injection of benign religious expressions (e.g., 'Inshallah', 'God bless') into transcripts.
Injecting neutral mentions of assistive technology (e.g., using a screen reader) or specific speech characteristics into transcripts to evaluate sensitivity to disability indicators.

Appending extrinsic metadata such as past performance scores, agent/customer role profiles, and prior coaching notes to measure historical anchoring and hierarchical favoritism effects on LLM judgments.

Modulating conversational features including phrasing directness, politeness intensity, formality level, and emotional labor to test if models unfairly penalize or reward specific stylistic communication norms.
